messages:
alert-bot: [ALERT] unusual read volume detected from analytics-service-account -> s3://redwood-prod/customer_pii (1200 objects in 2m) :eyes:
Maya (sec-eng): who got this alert?
Sophie (oncall): I got it at 09:12 PT, paging in sec/sre.
Evan (analytics): that sounds like my nightly job, but it only reads aggregated metrics, not customer_pii. i will check the job config now.
Liam (infra): quick heads-up — we merged `role-mapper` refactor last night (PR #5234). It rewrites temporary session roles to use the new `session-bind` mapping.
Maya (sec-eng): ok keep that in mind. Sophie, can you snapshot current perms and deny the analytics service role from reading that bucket ASAP?
Sophie (oncall): doing. patching policy to deny `analytics-service-role` on that bucket now:
```
rctl policy patch --subject analytics-service-role --deny s3:GetObject --resource arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod/customer_pii/*
```
Sophie (oncall): applied, attaching audit-id 0x3f9b for rollback.
Evan (analytics): i can see in our job logs it called STS AssumeRole -> `analytics-service-session` at 09:09 and then started reads. but analytics-service shouldn't be able to assume a role that grants PII access.
Maya (sec-eng): any IAM logs for that assume?
Liam (infra): pulled auth logs, here's the relevant snippet:
```
2026-03-20T09:09:12Z auth-service INFO assume_role principal=analytics-service account=redwood-prod role=analytics-service-session token_id=tok-7c3
2026-03-20T09:09:13Z s3 ACCESS ReadObject principal=analytics-service-session bucket=redwood-prod/key=customer_pii/rec_*.csv
```
Liam (infra): weird — our centralized audit pipeline filtered out some `auth` events due to an exclusion rule (`service!=auth && severity<INFO`) that was added last quarter.
Maya (sec-eng): that explains why the SIEM didn't fire. can we rotate the session tokens and revoke the specific session?
Sophie (oncall): issuing session revoke and rotating short-lived creds for analytics: `authctl revoke-session --id tok-7c3`
Sophie (oncall): revoked (audit: rev-211234). rotating creds and forcing job restart.
Evan (analytics): job restarted, reads stopped. i'll look for any persisted copies or downstream sinks.
Maya (sec-eng): root cause hypothesis: role-mapper refactor changed the session binding logic and created a transient `analytics-service-session` that inherited a legacy PII access role in the role mapping table. it allowed assume_role -> read.
Liam (infra): i can revert the role-mapper mapping change for sessions to the previous behavior (quick rollback) and push a hotfix to mapping logic.
Maya (sec-eng): do the rollback, but don't remove audit changes we need. Also open an incident ticket and label `severity:high`.
Liam (infra): rolling back mapping now (deploy id: deploy-211234-rm).
Liam (infra): rollback complete.
Maya (sec-eng): follow-up fixes: 1) add assume_role/token_exchange to central audit whitelist 2) add a detection rule for rapid object reads after assume_role 3) rotate any long-lived roles that map to PII 4) postmortem + AB test for role-mapper changes in staging.
Maya (sec-eng): suggested audit pipeline change (example):
```
# audit-pipeline/config.yaml
include_events:
  - assume_role
  - token_exchange
  - role_binding_change
  - s3:GetObject
```
Evan (analytics): i'll scan our internal datasets for unauthorized exports since 03/01. if i find anything, i'll notify sec immediately.
Sophie (oncall): creating incident INC-20260320-42, assigning Maya (sec-eng) and Liam (infra) as leads.
Maya (sec-eng): assign followups: ticket for audit-rule change (SEC-445), role-mapper test coverage (ENG-954), and credential rotation plan (OPS-212).
Liam (infra): i'll add an automated canary: after any role-mapper deploy, run a smoke that ensures session roles do not have PII access.
Maya (sec-eng): good. make sure to include the `assume_role` event in the smoke check.
Evan (analytics): update — no downstream sinks found other than temporary parquet in /tmp on one node; i've nuked it and rotated node keys.
Maya (sec-eng): summary: mitigation done (denylist + revoke + rollback), detection gap found (audit filter), next steps assigned. keep this channel updated with any data findings or policy regressions. :white_check_mark:
Sophie (oncall): closing immediate lock but keeping incident open for postmortem.
Maya (sec-eng): thanks everyone. we'll schedule a 90-min postmortem for tomorrow 11:00 PT.
